markets.rules_primary: If Senate has conducted any recorded vote on the SAVE America Act after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This includes:
Roll call votes
Recorded votes
Yea-and-nay votes
Electronic votes (in the House)
Division/standing votes

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Voice votes where individual member positions are not recorded
Unanimous consent agreements without a recorded vote
Votes in committee, unless the bill/motion specifically refers to a committee vote
Procedural determinations by the presiding officer
Deemed passage without an actual vote

For clarity:
A vote on cloture regarding the bill/motion, including cloture on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion, DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on the rule governing debate of the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion if the bill/motion specifically refers to that rule
A vote on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on final passage DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on an amendment to the bill/motion does NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion unless the bill/motion specifically refers to that amendment
markets.title: Will the Senate vote on the SAVE America Act?

markets.rules_primary: If the United States has agreed to, signed, or accepted a new Iran-US nuclear deal before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An agreement also made with other countries (i.e. multilaterally) is still encompassed if the United States participates. "A new Iran-US nuclear deal" means a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both the United States and Iran that (1) imposes verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program, including limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations, AND (2) provides for the lifting, suspension, or modification of at least one US economic sanction on Iran in exchange for Iran's nuclear commitments.

Clarification (04/19/26): The Agreement Long rulebook variable defines the nature of the qualifying instrument: it must be a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both governments. It does not impose a precondition that the signing itself must occur before resolution. Because the Payout Criterion is satisfied if the United States has "agreed to, signed, or accepted" such an instrument, both governments publicly and officially agreeing to the terms of what will be a qualifying written agreement is sufficient to resolve the market to Yes, even if the formal signing has not yet taken place.

Clarification (06/02/26): A qualifying instrument must impose "verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program." A restriction is "verifiable" only where it establishes a concrete, objectively ascertainable standard (a defined limit, prohibition, quantity, or monitoring provision) against which compliance could in principle be confirmed; a general expression of intent that fixes no such standard is not considered “verifiable” for the purposes of this event. Accordingly, a bare pledge not to develop or pursue nuclear weapons, unaccompanied by any concrete limit on Iran's nuclear materials, activities, or facilities, does not on its own satisfy criterion (1). Conversely, a commitment to completely 'stop' or ‘suspend’ a specific nuclear activity (such as uranium enrichment) establishes a concrete prohibition (an implicit limit of zero) and qualifies as a restriction, whereas a vague promise to 'reduce' activities without a defined metric or monitoring mechanism does not. The enumerated examples (limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations) are illustrative and not exhaustive: a formal, verifiable commitment to remove, transfer, or cap Iran's stock of enriched uranium, confirmable by the receiving state or an oversight body, is a restriction on Iran's nuclear program and satisfies criterion (1). In every case, criterion (2) must independently be met.

Clarification (06/17/26): To clarify, the U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding reportedly now in effect does not satisfy criterion (1) of the definition of a "new Iran-US nuclear deal," and this market will therefore not resolve to Yes on the basis of that instrument at this time. The memorandum provides for the existing state of Iran's nuclear program to be maintained pending a subsequent agreement, and defers the disposition of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium to a mechanism to be mutually agreed in that subsequent agreement. That it states a minimum methodology for that future mechanism — down-blending on site under IAEA supervision — constrains the form of a mechanism yet to be agreed, but specifies no quantity, enrichment level, or completion deadline for the down-blending. An instrument that provides for maintaining Iran's nuclear program at an unspecified status quo, or that defers its substantive nuclear commitments to a subsequent agreement, does not by itself establish the concrete, objectively ascertainable standard that a "verifiable" restriction requires.
markets.subtitle: Before October
markets.title: Will the US agree to a new Iranian nuclear deal this year?

The following do NOT constitute a visit:

Flying over the area without landing
Layovers during which the person remains in an airplane
Virtual or remote appearances
Presence in international waters adjacent to the area
Presence solely within embassy or consulate grounds
Plans, announcements, or scheduling of future visits that do not occur during the applicable time period

For the avoidance of doubt, a visit occurs only when the person exits an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or train within the area, or otherwise physically enters the area not aboard one. Remaining aboard, including during flyovers, drive-throughs, and non-exit refueling stops, does not constitute a visit. Exiting within the area constitutes a visit regardless of duration or method of exit.
markets.title: Will María Corina Machado visit Venezuela before Oct 1, 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If the United States federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse of appropriations at 10:00 AM ET on Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A shutdown is defined as the government's orderly suspension of agency work that is not legally excepted, typically accompanied by furloughing the employees who perform that work, when funding is unavailable.

Examples that would resolve the market to Yes:

OMB releases a formal directive that orders heads of the affected agencies to "execute plans for an orderly shutdown," which is in effect as of 10:00 AM ET on Oct 1, 2026
OPM posts a current operating status that indicates that "due to a partial lapse in appropriations, Federal Government operations vary by agency"

Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:

A technical lapse in appropriations occurs, but OMB directs agencies to continue standard operations
Government closures or operating status changes resulting from Federal holidays, inclement weather, or other emergencies, unless such closures coincide with a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations
markets.title: Will the US government be shut down on Oct 1, 2026?

Treaties require two-thirds Senate approval for passage. The market resolves based on the first occurrence of the specified milestone.

markets.rules_primary: If legislation requiring California law enforcement agencies to delete automated license plate reader data held for more than 30 days becomes law in California before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The legislation must impose a retention limit of 30 days or less on automated license plate reader (ALPR) data held by California law enforcement agencies, as a general rule. It may carve out data that is part of an evidence file for an active investigation or criminal proceeding, or that matches a vehicle of interest list, and still qualify.

The bill number does not matter. SB 1013 (Cervantes) is the leading vehicle as of Issuance, but this market settles on the provision, not the vehicle. Legislation carrying the required provision counts whichever bill number it is enacted under, including if SB 1013 is renumbered, if its contents are amended into another bill, or if a different member introduces the provision.

Enactment means the legislation becomes California law, whether by the Governor's signature or by operation of law without signature, or by the Legislature overriding a veto.

markets.rules_primary: If the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $130000 starting Sep 22, 2026 and before Oct 1, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of distinct US states Donald Trump has visited (per VISITAREA rules) is at least 9 in Sep 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
VISITAREA contract: https://kalshi-public-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/contractterms/VISITAREA.pdf

The following do NOT constitute a visit:

Flying over the area without landing
Layovers during which the person remains in an airplane
Virtual or remote appearances
Presence in international waters adjacent to the area
Presence solely within embassy or consulate grounds
Plans, announcements, or scheduling of future visits that do not occur during the applicable time period

For the avoidance of doubt, a visit occurs only when the person exits an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or train within the area, or otherwise physically enters the area not aboard one. Remaining aboard, including during flyovers, drive-throughs, and non-exit refueling stops, does not constitute a visit. Exiting within the area constitutes a visit regardless of duration or method of exit.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of the 12 fiscal year 2027 regular appropriations bills that have become law is at least 5 before October 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each of the 12 regular appropriations categories is counted separately. 

A standalone appropriations law counts as one, while an omnibus or minibus counts once for each regular appropriations bill enacted within it; for example, a package containing four regular appropriations divisions counts as four. 

Continuing resolutions, supplemental appropriations, and other funding measures do not count unless they enact one or more of the 12 regular appropriations bills. A regular appropriations bill counts regardless of its legislative vehicle, bill number, or whether it is enacted as a division of a broader law.

For example, in FY2019 the applicable number is 5: two minibuses covering Energy-Water, Legislative Branch, Military Construction–VA, Defense, and Labor-HHS-Education were enacted before October 1.

markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. Census Bureau reports that U.S. private data center construction spending for August 2026 is above $85.0B (billion) at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market will resolve based on the first published estimate of U.S. private data center construction spending for August 2026 reported by the U.S. Census Bureau in its Value of Private Construction Put in Place – Seasonally Adjusted Annual Rate data.

The relevant figure is found under:

Private → Nonresidential → Office → Data center

The Census Bureau reports this figure in millions of dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR). For example, $70 billion corresponds to $70,000 million.

The first figure published for the relevant month will be used, including if Census identifies that figure as preliminary. Subsequent revisions, corrections, or updated estimates will not affect the market’s resolution.
